newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke says tax cuts not top budget priority.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says tax cuts not top budget priority.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said tax cuts were not his top priority for the November 26 budget that could decide the fate of the Conservative government.

In an interview with the Daily Telegraph, he said reducing government borrowing and maintaining essential public services were higher priorities in the lead-up to the budget, the last before a general election due by next May.

"Once we have ensured that borrowing is on course and ensured that we have met our obligations of high quality public services, then we will consider whether or not we can pursue our tax policies and our 20 percent standard rate objective.

"But that is the order in which I shall appproach things. The Conservative Party cannot and will not, proceed on the basis that we approach the budget in November as some populist means of getting re-elected and then produce some sort of budget after the election, which tries to sort it out.
"So if -- and I stress the if -- there are any tax cuts they will be tax cuts, which I have completely satisfied myself will not have to be reversed thereafter."
